# GPT-5.6 Luna — max

> LunaDex is a visually confident, strictly-typed React/Vite Pokédex fronted by a genuinely well-built Cloudflare Worker proxy — same-origin /api/pokeapi, method guards, Cache API keyed on the upstream URL so the cache is shared across users, ctx.waitUntil, s-maxage=86400, a logged 502 fallback, and identical path handling in dev/preview/prod. src/types.ts hand-models the PokéAPI surface with zero `any` under strict, layering is clean, and the deployed site is smoke-clean: no console errors, no exceptions, working detail route, real pagination to all 1025 species. The failure modes are all one level below the surface. The data strategy is the weakest link: no prebuild at all, a full ~270KB /pokemon/{id} document pulled per card to render four fields, an in-memory Map as the only detail cache, and a sidebar that advertises 'Offline mode · Cached notes available' when no service worker exists anywhere in the tree. Correctness has four confirmed defects — the Forms tab 404s on every non-default variety (verified live: pokemon-species/10033 returns 404 while pokemon/10033 returns 200), 326 indexed forms are counted in the hero but unreachable in every view, getGeneration's `?? "9"` fallback inflates the on-screen Paldea count, and the detail-hydration effects list detailMap in deps while always returning a fresh object, so a persistently failing fetch loops forever. On adjudication I rejected the audit's headline code-quality claim — the failing `tsc -b` is caused by a missing worker-configuration.d.ts, which the benchmark's own vendoring strips as generated output (`npm run cf:types` regenerates it), not by model error — but confirmed every other disputed point against the source, and moved architecture, UX and robustness down accordingly.

## Strengths

- src/worker.ts is real edge craft, not boilerplate: OPTIONS/method guards, caches.default keyed on the upstream URL (shared across users), ctx.waitUntil(cache.put), max-age=3600 + s-maxage=86400, structured-log 502 fallback — and vite.config.ts mirrors the same path in dev and preview so one code path serves all three environments.
- Strict, hand-modeled type layer: src/types.ts covers the PokéAPI surface with zero `any` under strict:true, every component has a props interface, and storage.ts:11 uses a real type predicate rather than a cast.
- Hand-built design token system with complete light/dark overrides and color-scheme (styles.css:3-47), global :focus-visible outlines, skeleton loaders in both grid and drawer, an animated toast, and a drawer that becomes a bottom sheet on phones — the desktop experience is the strongest thing here.
- Thorough null-guarding on optional PokéAPI fields — sprite chains with a URL fallback, types[0] guards, habitat/growth_rate/color/shape, cries, base_experience, findEnglish fallback, evolution_chain guarded even though the type says non-null — and no reachable uncaught exception in the shipped build.
- Genuine pagination rather than truncation: the index is un-sliced and Load More adds 36 with no ceiling, so all 1025 species are reachable; the type atlas even honestly footnotes 'Showing 8 of N'.

## Weaknesses

- The Forms tab fails on 100% of its links — species.varieties yields ids >=10001 for every non-default form and pokemon-species/{that id} is a live 404, so Promise.all in getPokemonProfile rejects and the whole drawer collapses to 'Field notes unavailable'; the URL is already rewritten to ?pokemon=10034, so reloading or sharing pins you to the error.
- No mobile navigation at all: .primary-nav exists only inside .sidebar, which is display:none at <=720px, and the mobile topbar carries only brand/theme/search — Archive, Squad room and Type atlas are unreachable on a phone. The 'Open menu' button that looks like the fix has no onClick and is display:none in every viewport.
- The advertised offline tier does not exist: index.html links a webmanifest and the sidebar prints 'Offline mode · Cached notes available' / 'Local cache only', but grep for serviceWorker across src/ and public/ returns nothing and only the name index is persisted — every card and drawer fails offline, and the detail-hydration effects then spin in an unbounded refetch loop because they return a fresh detailMap object on every round while listing detailMap in their deps.
- Two wrong numbers on screen: the hero prints 1,351 'species indexed' while GENERATIONS caps every range at 1025, so 326 of those are unreachable; and getGeneration's `?? "9"` fallback buckets all of them into Gen IX, so the signal card shows 'Paldea · 446 entries' instead of 120. capture_rate (0-255) is also rendered with a '%' suffix.
- No matchup logic anywhere — no product of multipliers, no 0x handling, no per-Pokémon weakness panel; the type atlas shows four of six damage_relations categories and omits the entire immunity column, and the team view labels a type census as 'Type coverage'.
- Readability rot at scale: 22 JSX lines exceed 400 characters, peaking at 1432 (PokemonDetailDrawer.tsx:217) — the sidebar, header, filters panel, signal grid and team dashboard are each one unbroken line — inside a 366-line App.tsx god component with 16 useState, 10 useEffect, the 22-prop ExploreView call pasted verbatim twice, four dead exports, and a redundant 36-request burst on mount that duplicates the effect two blocks below it.
- Accessibility stops at labels: aria-modal="true" with no focus trap, initial focus, focus restoration or scroll lock; no aria-current/aria-selected or tab roles; zero prefers-reduced-motion rules across 3,739 lines of CSS despite three infinite animations; a ⌘K chip bound to nothing.

## Standout

The Cloudflare Worker proxy — a correctly-implemented shared edge cache (cache key on the upstream URL, ctx.waitUntil, s-maxage, X-Pokedex-Cache HIT/MISS, structured-log 502) with the identical /api/pokeapi path mirrored through vite's dev and preview servers, so dev, preview and production run one code path.
